examples.japanese: {姪|めい}は{今年|ことし}{小学校|しょうがっこう}に{入学|にゅうがく}する。
examples.english: My niece is starting elementary school this year.

examples.japanese: {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}が{遊|あそ}びに{来|き}た。
{姪|めい}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}プレゼントを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a birthday present for my niece.

examples.japanese: {姪|めい}は{来年|らいねん}{中学生|ちゅうがくせい}になる。
examples.english: My niece will become a middle school student next year.

examples.japanese: {姉|あね}の{姪|めい}っ{子|こ}が{夏休|なつやす}みに{泊|と}まりに{来|く}るので、{部屋|へや}を{片付|かたづ}けなくてはいけない。
examples.english: My sister's daughter is coming to stay during summer vacation, so I need to tidy up the room.

notes:
{姪|めい} means niece — the daughter of one's brother or sister. Japanese does not distinguish between a brother's daughter and a sister's daughter; both are {姪|めい}.

FAMILY TERMS:
- {姪|めい}: niece
- {甥|おい}: nephew
- {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}: niece (casual, affectionate)
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}: nephew (casual, affectionate)

POLITE FORMS:
When referring to someone else's niece or nephew, add お〜さん:
- お{姪|めい}さん: your niece
- お{甥|おい}さん: your nephew

KANJI:
The kanji {姪|めい} uses the {女|おんな}へん radical. It is not used in other common words, so learners typically encounter it only in this family term.

USAGE:
In casual speech, {姪|めい}っ{子|こ} is more common than {姪|めい} alone, especially when talking affectionately about a young niece.
